- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for sudden reversal and reduce forecast 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast; if trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.5%.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; apply a 1–3% downward correction for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply, model may overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days to avoid “sentiment trap.”
